graphEvents.label: Additive design follows system-prompt injection point

label: The extension is additive because it rewrites the native system-prompt skills section; the advisor injects into the user turn (Pi transform, Claude additionalContext), so brief churn has no cached-prefix cost. REJECT porting additive-only semantics.

Advisor churn dedup is text-level only (Claude head-keep, Pi byte-identical suppress) and no surface measures top-skill flip rate per session; ADAPT by computing flip rate offline from existing skillLabel diagnostics.
Session memory that suppresses already-surfaced skills would weaken the brief because advisor briefs are user-turn attachments that compaction can drop; REJECT.
Very short follow-ups such as continue or do it fall below the prompt-policy floors and do not fire, so the prior brief in history carries the route; no change needed.

Mid-length follow-ups (fix that too; yes, apply the second option) fire context-free through work_intent or length_and_token and can contradict the prior brief; no advisor path reads prior turn content, while the extension sends up to 2,000 characters of previous reply plus past-turn summaries.

ADAPT a weak-follow-up guard (emit no brief when a weakly fired prompt's top skill is below the confidence bar) after a follow-up-pair benchmark confirms the harm; REJECT feeding previous-reply text into the lexical scorer, which pollutes lanes and breaks the exact-prompt cache key.
